summary: Bottom action bar position differs: React renders it pinned at the bottom of the viewport, Android renders it immediately below the message list (top-anchored), leaving a large empty cream/ivory area below.

summary: Form content is more vertically compressed on Android: Email/Password fields, social buttons, terms text, and 'Create One' link are rendered higher up the viewport, leaving more empty space at the bottom.
Typography on Android appears slightly larger/heavier: 'Sign In' heading and input labels look bigger than React's, contributing to the tighter vertical packing.

Footer links differ: React shows 'Forgot password?' (lowercase, underlined); Android shows 'Forgot Password?' (title case, underlined) and 'Create One' (title case) vs React's 'Create one' (lowercase).
Yellow header bar is narrower in height on Android (roughly 96px vs ~115px on React), and the RAFT logo+wordmark is scaled down and positioned with slightly different vertical centering.
Overall font rendering differs (sans-serif weight/spacing), causing label and link text widths to differ between platforms.
likelyCauses: Android uses different default font scaling or dp-based dimensions that produce larger text metrics for the same logical size.
Different vertical padding/margins in the Android layout (e.g., top safe-area handling or form section spacing) compress the form upward.
Footer capitalization is controlled per-platform (Android uses 'Forgot Password?' / 'Create One') rather than a shared i18n string.
suggestedFixes: Align Android form vertical padding/spacing to match React's baseline so the form sits at a similar y-offset within the 390x844 viewport.
Normalize label and heading text size/weight on Android to match React's typography scale.
Decide whether footer link casing ('Forgot Password?' / 'Create One') should be platform-specific or unified and document accordingly.
Adjust Android header banner height to match React's banner height.
intentional: Continue with GitHub button is black on Android and white on React; per artin's ruling the Android black treatment is correct and React will adopt later.

summary: Yellow RAFT hero band is significantly taller on React (occupies ~upper third) vs iOS (smaller band with more vertical breathing room).
Sign In title and form fields appear larger / heavier weight on iOS; React uses lighter typography at same logical sizes.
Vertical spacing between Email field, Password field, and Signing in… button is looser on iOS than React (more whitespace between rows).

Footer text wrap differs: React renders 'By continuing, you agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.' as a tight 3-line block; iOS wraps it across 2 lines with 'Terms of Service' and 'Privacy Policy' underlined as separate links.
React shows 'Forgot password?' link that is missing on the iOS render in this state.
likelyCauses: Different default type scale / line-height between React web stack and iOS UIKit rendering at the captured device resolution.
Different vertical rhythm tokens (form field gap, section spacing) between the two platforms' design implementations.
Footer legal copy is being split into 2 underlined links on iOS but rendered as a single underlined phrase on React.
suggestedFixes: Normalize the hero band height / padding-top so both platforms reserve the same proportional space below it.
Unify form vertical rhythm: set the same gap (e.g. 16/24dp) between Email, Password, primary button, and the OR divider on both sides.
Align the legal-text link treatment: decide whether 'Terms of Service' and 'Privacy Policy' are 2 distinct links or one inline phrase and apply consistently.
Decide whether 'Forgot password?' should appear in the signing-in disabled state on iOS as it does on React, or hide it on both.
Keep the GitHub black-button treatment as the intended product behavior on iOS/native and schedule the React web adoption separately.
intentional: GitHub social button rendered as black with white icon+text on iOS vs white-with-dark-text on React — native is the desired behavior (react-adopts-later).

summary: Header banner: on Android (left) the yellow RAFT banner sits flush against the left edge with the logo near the top-left corner; on iOS (right) the banner is narrower with visible side margins and the logo appears lower/centered-left.

likelyCauses: Kuikly layout not honoring platform-agnostic padding/safe-area insets, causing iOS to render content without left/right screen-edge bleed the Android build applies.
Header banner implemented with absolute positioning sized to Android dp values rather than relative/flex sizing, so it fails to scale on the larger iOS canvas.
Default iOS font scale (and Kuikly text style mapping) producing heavier/larger footer link rendering vs. Android.
Inconsistent vertical spacing tokens between Email, Password, and primary CTA across platforms.

summary: React view is significantly shorter (496px) and ends with the file attachment card and reaction toolbar; Android view extends to 844px and includes additional long inline-code wrap-test content not present in the React snapshot.

likelyCauses: React baseline crop was taken on the element-bounds contract at 496px height, truncating the message before the long-code/ellipsis sections; Android used a manual rect of full 844px including additional body content.

Avatar and header row layout differs between the two component implementations (spacing, font sizes, ellipsis behavior).
